headline: Calf return went cleanly (two easy runs, achilles 0, recovery flat); hold, with the calf-clear week next and strides returning on 25 Nov.
review_md:
# Weekly review — Sunday 8 November 2026

Shep — the return from the calf went as well as it could have: two clean easy runs, no symptoms. Hold.

## The week (2–8 Nov)

Planned: bike and isometrics to Friday, a return test on Saturday, a second run Sunday only if Saturday felt like nothing. Done: sauna and rest Monday, easy bike Tuesday, rest Wed/Thu (your daughter's graduation), gym Friday (chest, ski erg, leg work, no pain), **6.4 km easy Saturday** (HR 133, RPE 1) and **7.0 km easy Sunday** (HR 137, 5:09/km). About 13 km. The Sunday condition was met.

One loose end: I asked for the single-leg raises and hops result and the log never stated it. Two pain-free runs are better evidence than a note, so I'm not holding anything on it. Next time, one line in the log ("raises/hops clean") and I'll stop asking.

## Calf and achilles

Achilles 0 all week; no first-step or desk-chair stiffness mentioned. Calf: "no pain at all" after Saturday, and Sunday's run was even and uneventful on the numbers. That is two days, not a week. The rule stands: the November volume step and any speed wait for **a full week of normal running** that is calf-clear. The week starting tomorrow is that week.

The warning from 31 Oct still applies: the calf was fine in the warm-up and tightened inside 0.8 km. Runs three to five are the real test, not the first two.

## Recovery

HRV 7-day baseline 36.1, flat for three weeks: settled, not rebounded. RHR baseline 48.7, this week 47–48. Sleep 8.2 h, score 88. ACWR 0.4–0.6, deliberately low. Saturday's HRV of 34 coincides with the Guinness you flagged and was back to 36 on Sunday — an explained flat morning, left alone. Nothing here argues against rebuilding.

## Where this leaves the build

You are about 10 days behind the November shape agreed on 6 Oct. That is the cost of the calf and not worth chasing. Volume rises while running is almost all easy, and not in the same weeks as intensity, so:

- **9–15 Nov:** 36 km, all easy, flat, Vomeros. The calf-clear week.
- **16–22 Nov:** about 58 km, long run 16.
- **23–29 Nov:** about 54 km. Volume holds while strides return (4 x 15 s on Wednesday). Tempo waits until 5 Dec at the earliest.
- December resumes the climb once there is a month of calf-clear running. The under-2 km/week slope leaves room to absorb these 10 days before the March peak.

## Admin

**Linda Franks 5 entries open today at 12:00 and sold out in 2 h 20 min last year.** Enter now if you want the 17 Jan record attempt; whether it is raced as a record is decided later by how the calf and first quality weeks go. Wokingham Half (21 Feb) entry is still to make. Fission 20 opens 1 Jan.

## Recommendation: hold

Nothing already planned changes. The proposal adds 23–29 Nov (provisional) and carries the other two weeks forward. If any run this week shows calf tightness, stop, take the bike, and tell me; the build slides rather than being squeezed.

conversation.athlete_thoughts: Treadmill run today.. Thought I'd try running in the warm over the cold... Watch speed seemed out compared to treadmill. Ran 40mins at 6min km pace, as per treadmill. could feel the calf a tiny bit but nothing to say stop. Could have carried on.
conversation.coach_reply:
Shep — the treadmill was a reasonable call, and the calf note is the useful part of today.

**The pace mismatch.** Trust the belt, not the watch. Indoors the Garmin estimates speed from arm swing and cadence, and that estimate is uncalibrated, so it ran about 70 s/km fast against the belt (4:50 vs 6:00). That makes today's Garmin distance and pace wrong. The real figure is roughly 40 min at 6:00/km, about 6.5–7 km. The watch HR is still valid. If you want the treadmill logged cleanly, enter the belt distance in the log. It doesn't change anything about the load.

**The calf.** Today you could feel it a tiny amount. On Wed 11 Nov (7 km) you wrote "a tiny bit tight near the end". That is two flags in your last three runs (10, 11 and 13 Nov). Neither is a stop, and you were right not to stop. But on 1 Nov the calf was fine in the warm-up, then tightened and ended the run. In my 8 Nov review I called runs three to five the real test, and this is what that test looks like: a low-level signal that repeats. A repeating "tiny" is a load signal on this calf–achilles complex, and it shouldn't be read as "could have carried on". "Could have carried on" is also the exact judgement that went wrong in the old flare–return cycle. Achilles 0, HR 138–139 and RPE 1 are all good, so I'm not alarmed. I'm just not stacking more on top of it.

**What happens.** The week-of-clear-running condition is not met yet, because a calf you can feel doesn't count as clear. The November volume step stays on hold until it is. So tomorrow's 10 km becomes 6 km. Sunday's 12 km long run becomes rest or the bike, and Monday stays rest. If the calf is silent on Saturday and again on Tuesday, the 16–22 Nov week resumes as written (it already carries the step to ~55 km). If Saturday is felt again, stop at the first sign and go to the bike. A physio check is then worth a call, since this has now repeated across runs. The treadmill is unlikely to be the cause; a belt is, if anything, slightly kinder than road.

Please add one line to tomorrow's log: when in the run you noticed the calf (warm-up, middle, end) and whether it fades or builds. That tells me more than the score.
